newsitem.title: USA: Pitt-Des Moines guilty in 1993 building collapse.
newsitem.headline: Pitt-Des Moines guilty in 1993 building collapse.

text.p: A federal jury convicted Pitt-Des Moines Inc. of violating safety rules in a 1993 accident that killed two ironworkers.
The Pittsburgh-based company could be fined up to $500,000 for each of two misdemeanor counts. A sentencing date was not set.
"The PDM case is a tragic example of what can happen when basic precautions are not followed," Labour Secretary Alexis Herman said in a statement.

The Nov. 3, 1993, collapse of 60 structural steel beams and columns and metal decking and sheeting at the construction site for Chicago's new central Post Office killed two workers and injured five others.
Prosecutors said the company did not properly secure the steel beams or train workers.
Pitt-Des Moines said it would appeal.

"We deny wrongdoing in this tragic incident, and we believe that today's verdict will be overturned on appeal," Tom Lloyd, the company's general counsel, said in a statement. "We have a strong case and an excellent safety record, which we intend to defend vigorously."
